title: GCLI-36b: code-map git layer, ranking, caps, omissions, command and parity test
description:
Child of GCLI-36 (12a), second split confirmed by the leader on 2026-11-17. 12a-2 is the git-reading layer, candidate assembly, ranking, caps and omission rows, the glyph code-map command with its manifest entry, and the parity test, built on 12a-1's pure layer (GCLI-40). Implemented in opum-ai/glyph-cli#80.

Designed by opum-doc as DEC-216 (a7), 2026-11-17, VERBATIM as relayed:
"(a) Golden parity, with one condition. Commit the golden-generation script beside the goldens, with the pinned opum-cli SHA (dev 91542f4) as a constant in it. It must fetch opum-cli by ref into a scratch directory, run its producer read-only over the same fixtures, and write the goldens, so anyone can reproduce them byte for byte. The test fails if a golden's header pin differs from the script's constant. A pin moves only by re-running the script, in the same change. There is no cross-repository dependency in glyph's CI.
(b) Task text on stdin, capped at 20,000 characters. Over the cap is a usage error, never a silent truncation. Plus --source-ref and --repo. {pointers, omissions} is the envelope's `data` under kind `code-map.result`, keeping the frozen contract."

Pinned to opum-cli dev 91542f4ccf2da3574f34c2377c6a6e2b3abd1102; estimateTokens is Math.ceil(text.length / 4) over UTF-16 code units (opum-cli dev 093b0e9 src/adapters/instruction-blocks.ts:122-124). The 20,000-character cap counts UTF-16 code units, the producer's own .length measure, kept for parity.

acceptanceCriteria.text: glyph code-map emits exactly the seam {pointers, omissions} for task text, source ref and repository, registers its result kind in the help manifest, and ranks tiers 1, 2 and 4 by rank, then score, then path.
The 20-file and 2,000-token caps are held in glyph, an over-token pointer is skipped not fatal, and every dropped candidate and read bound is named in omissions.
A parity test compares bytes against goldens produced by opum-cli producer at the pinned commit over the same fixtures, and fails if the pin moves without the goldens.
The same repository state, source ref and task text yield byte-identical output; bun run check passes.

implementationNotes: THREE DEFECTS in opum-cli's deterministic producer (src/context/code-map.ts at 91542f4), ported as is for byte parity and pinned by tests or goldens; filing them upstream is opum-cli's. (1) QUADRATIC EXTRACTORS: pathsNamedIn runs its pattern over the whole text and is quadratic in a long unbroken token: about 13 ms per call at 5,000 characters, 200 ms at 20,000 (the producer's own bound), 5 s at 100,000; collectIdentifiers calls it again, so a hostile 20,000-character task text costs about 0.4 s before any git read (also noted on GCLI-38). (2) LEADING-DOT PATHS: the path pattern starts at a letter, digit, underscore or @, so .quest/tasks/A.json is read as quest/tasks/A.json, which the non-code prefix does not catch; and ../src/a.ts is kept as src/a.ts. (3) QUOTED NON-ASCII GREP PATHS: grepFiles and grepLines run git grep without core.quotepath=false (the diff reads set it), so a non-ASCII path found by identifier comes back quoted, for example the literal string "src/caf\303\251.ts". The producer emits that string as a pointer path with lineRanges [] (a whole file) for a file that does not exist; it takes a file-cap slot and token budget, and the real src/café.ts, which the branch diff still finds, loses the identifier evidence the quoted entry absorbed. Glyph pins its grep reads to core.quotepath=true and --no-color so the output matches the producer's goldens whatever the caller's git config (a hostile-config test proves it); the golden generator runs the producer with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1.

Landed via opum-ai/glyph-cli#80, squash e2137a8469e14eae45eec8281adc17f7cba73104. Opus reviewer unit: REQUEST CHANGES at 968a740 (one blocking finding: the grep reads depended on the caller's git config), then APPROVE at 7d609e66a7734d9121e4580b1b6505f4be0c4d99 after the confirmatory round. Check, Docs and Tracker integrity green on the PR head and on the dev push run. SIZE: +1,603/-10 on 13 files at first push (+1,718/-14 on 14 files in the squash), well over the ~400-line ceiling; the leader accepted it whole because tests, fixtures and goldens carry the bulk. CARRIED non-blocking items for the next PR that touches these files (GCLI-37 / 12b): (1) the test/parity.test.ts hostile-config test has no positive control: nothing inside it shows git actually read the hostile config, so if GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL were ignored it would still pass; add one assertion, for example git config core.quotepath reads false under that environment. (2) test/cli.test.ts: the over-cap test title still says characters, not UTF-16 code units. (3) README: the sentence that the code-map seam never reads the working tree history by default is imprecise; tier 2 reads HEAD implicitly, and what it never reads is uncommitted changes. (4) opum-doc is asked to confirm that the (a7) 20,000 characters means UTF-16 code units, as built for parity; no change until it answers. No ADR 0005 is expected here.

DEC-216 (a8), decided by opum-doc, VERBATIM as relayed: "DEC-216 (a7)'s \"20,000 characters\" means 20,000 UTF-16 code units (JavaScript string length). That keeps glyph byte-identical to how opum-cli's producer slices the text, and parity is the point of (a7). glyph-cli's build, its usage message and its boundary tests stand as built." This answers carried item (4) in the close-out note above, which is dropped from the carried list; the other three carried items (the hostile-config positive control, the cli.test.ts over-cap title, the README wording) stay with GCLI-37.
